java-outdated-version.title: Application targets Java 8, which is end-of-life for free Oracle builds and below the Java 17 LTS baseline required for modern Azure Java workloads
java-outdated-version.description: The project configures sourceCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_1_8 in build.gradle. Java 8 is out of mainstream support (Oracle) and incompatible with many modern libraries and Azure services that require Java 17 or 21. Upgrade to Java 21 LTS (recommended) or Java 17 LTS.

legacy-http-client.title: Usage of java.net.HttpURLConnection — replace with java.net.http.HttpClient (Java 11+)
legacy-http-client.description: The application uses HttpURLConnection, a blocking, low-level HTTP API from Java 1.1. Java 11 introduced java.net.http.HttpClient, which supports HTTP/2, async execution, and modern timeout handling. Migrating reduces boilerplate and improves cloud-native compatibility.

no-structured-logging.title: Application logs using System.out.println — no structured logging framework configured
no-structured-logging.description: The application writes all log output via System.out.println with a custom timestamp prefix. Cloud-native workloads running on Azure App Service, AKS, or Azure Container Apps benefit from structured (JSON) logging using SLF4J + Logback or Log4j2, which integrates with Azure Monitor and Application Insights log ingestion.

no-health-check-endpoint.title: No HTTP health check endpoint exposed — required for container orchestration liveness and readiness probes
no-health-check-endpoint.description: The application does not expose any HTTP endpoint for health checking. Azure App Service, AKS, and Azure Container Apps rely on liveness and readiness probes to determine pod/instance health. Without a probe endpoint the platform cannot restart unhealthy instances or route traffic correctly.

no-observability.title: No metrics or distributed tracing instrumentation — required for Azure Monitor integration
no-observability.description: The application does not include any metrics (Micrometer, Prometheus) or distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry, Application Insights SDK) instrumentation. Cloud deployments on Azure benefit from automatic telemetry via the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro or Application Insights Java agent.

hardcoded-service-urls.title: Service endpoint URLs contain hard-coded hostnames that assume Docker network naming — use Azure service discovery or environment variables
hardcoded-service-urls.description: The configuration file batchscheduler.properties contains hard-coded hostnames such as zavainterestcalculator:8080, zavastatementservice:8080, and zavaledger:8080. These are Docker Compose internal DNS names and will not resolve in Azure Container Apps or AKS without corresponding service definitions. Use Azure service discovery (internal Kubernetes DNS) or inject URLs from environment variables / Azure App Configuration.

plaintext-credentials-in-config.title: Database credentials stored as plain text in batchscheduler.properties — use Azure Key Vault or managed identity
plaintext-credentials-in-config.description: The file src/main/resources/batchscheduler.properties contains a plain-text database password (db.****** Committing credentials to source control violates secret management best practices. Use Azure Key Vault references, managed identity authentication against Azure SQL, or environment-variable injection from a secrets store.

no-tls-for-service-calls.title: HTTP (not HTTPS) used for calls to downstream services — all inter-service traffic is unencrypted
no-tls-for-service-calls.description: The base URLs in batchscheduler.properties use the http:// scheme for interest, statement, and reconciliation services. In a production cloud environment inter-service traffic should be encrypted with TLS (https://). Azure Container Apps and AKS support automatic mTLS; at minimum, configure services to use HTTPS endpoints.

gradle-shadow-plugin-upgrade.title: Shadow plugin 7.1.2 is incompatible with Gradle 8+ — upgrade to Shadow 8.x before upgrading Gradle
gradle-shadow-plugin-upgrade.description: The project uses com.github.johnrengelman.shadow version 7.1.2. This version is incompatible with Gradle 8 and above due to removed Convention API. Upgrade to Shadow 8.3.x (or the GradleUp/shadow fork) before migrating to a current Gradle wrapper.

no-gradle-wrapper.title: No Gradle wrapper (gradlew) committed — builds are tied to the system Gradle version, causing reproducibility issues
no-gradle-wrapper.description: The repository does not include a gradlew wrapper script or gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties. Without the wrapper, CI/CD builds depend on the Gradle version installed on the build agent, which can lead to version drift and build failures. Run gradle wrapper --gradle-version 8.x to generate it.

unused-dependency.title: Declared dependency com.rabbitmq:amqp-client is not used in any source file
unused-dependency.description: build.gradle declares implementation 'com.rabbitmq:amqp-client:5.21.0' but no import or usage of the RabbitMQ client API was found in the source tree. Removing unused dependencies reduces the fat-JAR size, lowers transitive vulnerability exposure, and speeds up build resolution.

properties.description: Scheduled batch processor that triggers nightly financial operations (interest accrual, statement generation, daily reconciliation) against downstream microservices and logs run status to SQL Server.

security.name: Hardcoded database password in source-controlled properties file
security.description: The file src/main/resources/batchscheduler.properties commits a plain-text database password (db.****** to the repository. Any developer or CI agent with repository read access obtains the credential. Rotate the password immediately, remove it from version control history, and use Azure Key Vault or managed identity for SQL Server authentication.

security.name: Unencrypted HTTP used for all inter-service communication
security.description: All three downstream service endpoints (interest, statement, reconciliation) are contacted over plain HTTP. In transit the request payloads and any response data are exposed to network-level sniffing. Switch to HTTPS endpoints and enable certificate validation.

security.name: No authentication on outbound HTTP service calls
security.description: Calls to interest accrual, statement generation, and reconciliation services are made with no Authorization header or API key. Any service accessible from the batch scheduler network can be invoked without proof of identity. Add Azure Managed Identity-based authentication (OAuth 2.0 bearer token) or a shared API key passed via environment variable.
